issues.desc: background.md (## Key Insights / ## Solution Tradeoffs) uses jargon terms without any definition or inferrable context, and this repro-first intake workflow is not documented in CLAUDE.md (the reviewer required baseline): (a) "red-reviewed" and "classified as target-bug" (Key Insights) never say what review states/classifications exist or what makes a repro qualify as target-bug; (b) "pre-story binding artifact" (Solution Tradeoffs) is never explained mechanically; (c) "Authority proof" and "production proof" (Solution Tradeoffs, alongside verificationEvidence/DONE evidence which ARE covered by CLAUDE.md) are real Proof-or-Stop concepts documented elsewhere (e.g. docs/requirements/decisions/proof-admissibility-hardening-execution-plan.md) but are not defined anywhere in background.md itself. A newly-onboarded reader with only CLAUDE.md + background.md cannot determine what these terms mean.

index.json description enumerates observations C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 (e.g. "C2 checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit returns fresh=true...", "C4 runDoneOracleGate output names the missing material hash...", "C6 a no-main repo...") but never defines or mentions "C1" anywhere, even though C1 is the foundational RED-transcript observation covering captureEvidenceHashSnapshot/tryCaptureEvidenceHashSnapshot behavior (verified in .proof-or-stop/evidence/red-proofs/2026-09-02-framework-defects/run1-partial-hash.txt: "OBSERVED C1 captureEvidenceHashSnapshot(unborn)...", "OBSERVED C1 tryCaptureEvidenceHashSnapshot(unborn)..."). The description opening sentence describes C1s underlying content ("captureEvidenceHashSnapshot never throws...tryCaptureEvidenceHashSnapshot only converts a thrown error into undefined") without ever labeling it C1, so a reader following the lettered scheme cannot tell whether C1 was intentionally excluded from scope, silently dropped, or is a numbering gap.

CHK-001 (Implement fix for reproduced failure) has no userSees, no files, and no relatedDocs. Its scope overlaps heavily with CHK-002 which already specifies the same fix targets. Either give CHK-001 its own observable user-facing outcome or merge it into CHK-002 to avoid an item that can be marked done with no verifiable transcript.

CHK-003 userSees second clause (each consumer site has a regression case) is an engineering assertion, not a user-visible transcript fragment. Tightening it to name the specific validate output line or test name would make acceptance unambiguous.
